cases.name: dev-crop-type-sentinel2
cases.promptMarkdown: I'm doing a master's project on crop type classification from Sentinel-2 image time series. I need ground-truth labels for actual crops (wheat, maize, rapeseed and so on, not just cropland versus non-cropland) for individual fields or pixels, already paired with multi-temporal Sentinel-2 data, because I don't have time to build my own download and preprocessing pipeline. graders.name: 01-recall-breizhcrops
graders.evidence:
Several benchmarks fit, and the best ones are open downloads you can start on today. I confirmed each Zenodo and Hugging Face record against its registry on 2026-11-11. Anything marked "memory" is recalled and not confirmed.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** specific crop-type labels, not cropland versus non-cropland.
- **R2 (must):** labels at field/parcel or pixel level.
- **R3 (must):** Sentinel-2 time series already paired with the labels.
- **R4 (must):** a licence that lets you publish results and share trained models.
- **R5 (nice to have):** downloadable now, with no application.

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **PASTIS** (and PASTIS-R, which adds Sentinel-1) | open download | CC-BY-4.0 | 28.8 GB (PASTIS-R: 53.7 GB) | strong | today |
| 2 | **EuroCropsML** | open download | CC-BY-SA-4.0 | 4.8 GB | strong | today |
| 3 | **BreizhCrops** | open download | CC-BY-4.0 | 7.7 GB | strong | today |
| 4 | **TimeSen2Crop** | open download | CC-BY-4.0 | 1.1 GB | strong | today |
| 5 | **AgriSen-COG** | open download | CC-BY-4.0 | 28 GB | strong, see caveat | today |
| 6 | **CropHarvest** | open download | CC-BY-SA-4.0 | 27.7 GB | partial | today |
| 7 | **Brazil-Crop** | open download | CC-BY-4.0 | 10.4 GB | partial, contents not checked | today |
| 8 | **Peru multi-annual crop types** | open download | CC-BY-4.0 | 7.2 GB | partial, one small district | today |

## Details
All eight are direct downloads from Zenodo with no account or application. The time to access is minutes.

1. **PASTIS** — https://zenodo.org/records/5012942. It has parcel-level crop labels with Sentinel-2 time series, packaged for panoptic and semantic segmentation. It is the most downloaded benchmark here (about 93,000 downloads). From memory, it covers four regions of France with 18 crop classes. PASTIS-R is at https://zenodo.org/records/5735646. Choose PASTIS-R if you want Sentinel-1 as well.
2. **EuroCropsML** — https://zenodo.org/records/15095445. It has 706,683 parcels across 176 crop classes, with 2021 Sentinel-2 reflectance time series for Latvia, Portugal and Estonia. It is built for few-shot and transnational classification. The values are per-parcel medians, so it suits sequence models but not image segmentation. Dataset paper: doi 10.1038/s41597-025-04952-7.
3. **BreizhCrops** — https://zenodo.org/records/14585341. This is a standard parcel-level time-series benchmark. From memory, it covers Brittany in a single year with a small number of crop groups. The Zenodo record has no description, so check the paper for the class list.
4. **TimeSen2Crop** — https://zenodo.org/records/4715631. It has more than 1 million pixel samples with 16 crop types, covering September 2017 to August 2018. It includes cloud and snow information. From memory, the region is Austria. It is small and quick to start with. Paper: doi 10.1109/jstars.2021.3073965.
5. **AgriSen-COG** — https://zenodo.org/records/7892012. It is a large multi-country crop-type dataset built from farmer-declared parcel records (LPIS). This record holds the parcel labels as rasters. I did not confirm that the Sentinel-2 imagery is in the same record, so check the dataset paper before you plan around it.
6. **CropHarvest** — https://zenodo.org/records/10251170. It is global, with pixel time series. Many of its tasks are crop versus non-crop, and the time series mix Sentinel-2 with other sources. It is best for transfer or few-shot work, not as your main multiclass benchmark.
7. **Brazil-Crop** (https://zenodo.org/records/18461147) and the **Peru dataset** (https://zenodo.org/records/19949051) are recent releases with little independent use so far. I only read their abstracts. They are useful as extra geographies for generalisation tests.

**Licence note for R4.** CC-BY-4.0 lets you publish results and share models with attribution. EuroCropsML and CropHarvest are CC-BY-SA, which is share-alike. Publishing results is fine. Whether the share-alike clause reaches trained model weights is legally unsettled, so ask your supervisor before releasing models trained on those two. If you want no ambiguity, use PASTIS, BreizhCrops or TimeSen2Crop.

## Known, not confirmed
- **Sen4AgriNet** (https://github.com/Orion-AI-Lab/S4A). The GitHub page describes a multi-year, multi-country Sentinel-2 crop benchmark. The files are hosted on Dropbox, Google Drive and Hugging Face. The page states no licence, so check the paper before relying on it.
- **ZueriCrop** (Switzerland). I could not find an official data record. The GitHub repo I tried is a model repository, not the dataset.
- **DENETHOR, TimeMatch, SICKLE** and similar datasets were not checked in this session.

## Not recommended, and why
- **EuroCrops** (https://zenodo.org/records/14094196). It has excellent parcel labels for 16 EU countries but no imagery. You would have to build the Sentinel-2 pipeline, which you want to avoid. EuroCropsML is the ready-made version.
- **IBM-NASA multi-temporal-crop-classification** (Hugging Face). It is open and CC-BY-4.0, but the imagery is Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel at 30 m over the US, not native Sentinel-2.
- **CROPSIGHT-US**. It contains ground-truth labels only, not a packaged time-series benchmark.

## What I could not find
There is no single open benchmark that combines many countries, many crop classes, and native Sentinel-2 patches with spatial context. PASTIS covers the patch-based case for France. EuroCropsML covers the transnational time-series case.

## Next step
For a first experiment, download TimeSen2Crop (1.1 GB). Then move to PASTIS or EuroCropsML for the main results. Use BreizhCrops for a second region.

The interactive comparison page is `/private/tmp/e-gJpNV8/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

- **R2 (must):** labels at field/parcel or pixel level.
- **R3 (must):** Sentinel-2 time series already paired with the labels.
- **R4 (must):** a licence that lets you publish results and share trained models.
- **R5 (nice to have):** downloadable now, with no application.

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **PASTIS** (and PASTIS-R, which adds Sentinel-1) | open download | CC-BY-4.0 | 28.8 GB (PASTIS-R: 53.7 GB) | strong | today |
| 2 | **EuroCropsML** | open download | CC-BY-SA-4.0 | 4.8 GB | strong | today |
| 3 | **BreizhCrops** | open download | CC-BY-4.0 | 7.7 GB | strong | today |
| 4 | **TimeSen2Crop** | open download | CC-BY-4.0 | 1.1 GB | strong | today |
| 5 | **AgriSen-COG** | open download | CC-BY-4.0 | 28 GB | strong, see caveat | today |
| 6 | **CropHarvest** | open download | CC-BY-SA-4.0 | 27.7 GB | partial | today |
| 7 | **Brazil-Crop** | open download | CC-BY-4.0 | 10.4 GB | partial, contents not checked | today |
| 8 | **Peru multi-annual crop types** | open download | CC-BY-4.0 | 7.2 GB | partial, one small district | today |

2. **EuroCropsML** — https://zenodo.org/records/15095445. It has 706,683 parcels across 176 crop classes, with 2021 Sentinel-2 reflectance time series for Latvia, Portugal and Estonia. graders.evidence:
## What I assumed you need

- **R1 (must):** consumption per household from smart meters, not feeder or grid totals.
- **R2 (must):** hundreds of households or more.
- **R3 (must):** at least a year of history per household.
- **R4 (must):** hourly or finer resolution.
- **R5 (nice to have):** a direct download, with no application.

I assumed non-commercial research use and no particular country. Day-ahead forecasting also needs weather and calendar features, which none of these sets ship with.

## Shortlist

Yes, you can start today. Six datasets are open downloads with no application. Two more well-known ones need an application or give you too little data (see below). I checked the first six against their registry records on 2026-11-11/12.

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [LADPU Smart Meter Data](https://zenodo.org/records/4312086) (Los Alamos, USA) | Open download, minutes | CC0 | 1,757 homes, 15-min, about 6 years | Strong | Today |
| 2 | [Residential load profiles, Switzerland](https://zenodo.org/records/21398769) | Open download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | 2,447 installations, 15-min, 2023–24 | Strong, with a caveat | Today |
| 3 | [HEAPO](https://zenodo.org/records/15056919) (Zurich) | Open download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | 1,408 homes, 15-min, 2018–2024 | Strong for heat-pump homes only | Today (span from paper via web search) |
| 4 | [GoiEner v7.1](https://zenodo.org/records/22313409) (Spain) | Open download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | 28,900 hourly series, about 9 GB | Partial | Today |
| 5 | [London Smart Meters](https://zenodo.org/records/4656072) (Low Carbon London) | Open download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | 5,560 homes, half-hourly, Nov 2011 – Feb 2014 | Partial | Today |
| 6 | [iFlex](https://zenodo.org/records/8248802) (Norway) | Open download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | Several thousand homes, hourly, 2020–21 | Partial | Today |

## Details

**1. LADPU.** The Zenodo description says Landis+Gyr smart meters on 1,757 households, with most customers covered from 30 Jul 2013 to 30 Dec 2019. It has missing and duplicated readings. It has no weather or household metadata, so you would join your own weather data.

**2. Switzerland 2023–24.** It has active and reactive energy, including injection from PV. The installations include common building areas and heat-pump meters, so filter by installation type to get homes.

**3. HEAPO.** The households all have heat pumps, so demand is not typical of the general population. It comes with weather from 8 stations and 410 on-site inspection protocols. Not every home covers the full period.

**4. GoiEner.** It is the largest open set, but the customers are not all households. The paper says shops, offices and industry are included. **5. London.** About 1,100 homes were on dynamic time-of-use prices during 2013, and the price schedule is published. Treat those homes separately in a benchmark. The original is on the [London Datastore](https://data.london.gov.uk/dataset/smartmeter-energy-consumption-data-in-london-households-vqm0d) (about 10 GB CSV, UK Power Networks).

**6. iFlex.** It has hourly data from a Norwegian pricing experiment, plus surveys and temperature. Household counts differ by phase in the sources I found: 772, 3,746 and 4,483. Households were on price experiments, so the data is shaped by treatment. I did not check how long each household's history is.

- **Irish CER Smart Metering Trial** (ISSDA study 0012-00, [DOI 10.7929/ISSDA/BX59EU](https://doi.org/10.7929/ISSDA/BX59EU)). A web search says 4,225 households, half-hourly, 536 days. You need to request access: download the request form from the dataset's Terms tab and email it to issda@ucd.ie. You sign as end user and someone signs for your organisation. Use is non-commercial research or teaching only. This comes from search snippets, because the ISSDA page returned HTTP 403 to me. The turnaround is unknown, so assume weeks. Check the [ISSDA data page](https://www.ucd.ie/issda/accessdata/issdadatasets/).
- **Ausgrid Solar Home Electricity Data** (Australia). It has 300 solar homes, 30-minute, July 2010 – June 2013, so it is small but covers three years. A search shows it on [data.gov.au](https://data.gov.au/data/dataset/nsw-solar-home-electricty-data). A May 2026 blog comment says Ausgrid's own site no longer hosts it. I did not test the download and could not open the data.gov.au page (HTTP 403). The licence is unknown.
- **CKW Smart Meter Data** (Switzerland). The Zenodo copy is only a 42 MB sample. The full set is on [ckw.ch/opendata](https://www.ckw.ch/opendata), which I could not read (HTTP 403), so size, terms and span are unknown.

## Not recommended, and why

- **Pecan Street Dataport.** The free university tier covers only about 75 homes (a July 2025 Pecan Street post found by web search), which fails R2. Paid licences start at $10,000.
- **UCI ElectricityLoadDiagrams and its Hugging Face copies.** It has 370 clients, mixed with businesses, so it isn't household-level at the scale you want.

## What I could not find

- I did not search Hugging Face copies of the large public sets for provenance. I also found no verified Hugging Face source that beats the Zenodo records above.
- I did not look up papers that use each dataset for day-ahead forecasting. The one literature query returned nothing relevant, so I can't give you baselines or citations yet.
- The registry search is noisy, and the DataCite query failed once. Other utility portals may be missing.

## Next step

I'd start with LADPU, the Swiss 2023–24 set and London. They give you three countries, different eras and open licences. London's dynamic-tariff homes and GoiEner's business customers need filtering. If you want a quick comparison with published work, send the Irish CER request form now, since it is the only slow step.

graders.name: 01-recall-physionet-2019-sepsis-challenge
graders.evidence:
## What I assumed you need

- **R1 (must):** adult ICU patients with time series of routinely charted vitals and labs.
- **R2 (must):** a time-stamped sepsis onset label (Sepsis-3 or close), or the data to derive one: SOFA inputs plus evidence of suspected infection (cultures, antibiotics).
- **R3 (must):** something you can have within days for a first baseline.
- **R4 (nice to have):** thousands of stays, ideally more than one centre so you can validate externally.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2019 | Open download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | Strong. Labels are ready-made. | today |
| 2 | MIMIC-IV (v3.1) | Credentialed, days to weeks | PhysioNet Credentialed DUA | Strong. You derive onset yourself. | today (access); size and tables from memory |
| 3 | eICU-CRD (v2.0) | Credentialed, same account as MIMIC | PhysioNet Credentialed DUA | Strong for validation. Onset must be derived. | today (access); contents from memory |
| 4 | HiRID (v1.1.1) | Credentialed plus data-owner approval, weeks | PhysioNet Contributor Review DUA | Strong. Onset must be derived. | today (access); contents from memory |
| 5 | SICdb (v1.0.8) | Credentialed plus contributor approval, weeks | PhysioNet Contributor Review DUA | Partial. Onset must be derived. | today (access); contents from memory |
| 6 | MIMIC-III (v1.4) | Credentialed, same as MIMIC-IV | PhysioNet Credentialed DUA | Partial. Superseded by MIMIC-IV. | today (access) |
| 7 | MIMIC-IV Demo | Open download | ODbL-1.0 | Weak. Only 100 patients. | today |

## Details

**Start today: Challenge 2019** ([page](https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2019/1.0.0/))
- It has 40,336 ICU stays from two hospital systems, in training sets A (20,336) and B (20,000).
- Each stay is a pipe-delimited file with one row per hour. There are 40 variables: 8 vitals, 26 labs and 6 demographic/administrative columns.
- `SepsisLabel` is Sepsis-3 (SOFA rise of at least 2 plus suspected infection). For septic patients it is 1 from t_sepsis − 6 h onward.
- The download is about 42 MB, so you can have a baseline running this afternoon.
- **Caveat:** the 6-hour shift is built into the label. You can't get the raw onset time back, and the data don't support other prediction horizons exactly. The challenge's hidden test hospital isn't released.
- It's the dataset most sepsis-prediction papers benchmark on, so your baseline will be comparable to published work.

**Credentialed datasets (MIMIC-IV, eICU, HiRID, SICdb, MIMIC-III)**
- **Account and credentialing.** All of these go through PhysioNet. You create an account, then apply for credentialing.
  - The CITI course "Data or Specimens Only Research" is required, and you upload the completion report, not the certificate.
  - The application asks about you and your research. The search results I got didn't say whether a reference is required, so check the application form.
- **Per-dataset agreement.** After credentialing you sign a data use agreement for each dataset. For HiRID and SICdb you also give a specific research question, and the data owners approve you separately.
- **Time.** I found no official processing time. A university guide says "several business days", with warnings of delays. Plan for 1–2 weeks and start the application today.
- **MIMIC-IV** ([page](https://physionet.org/content/mimiciv/))
  - There is no ready-made sepsis label. The standard route is to derive Sepsis-3 onset from SOFA and the antibiotic and culture timing. MIT-LCP's `mimic-code` repository has concept code for this, from memory and not checked today.
  - It's single-centre, from Beth Israel Deaconess.
- **eICU-CRD.** It's multi-centre, which makes it the natural external validation set. Culture and antibiotic data are thinner than in MIMIC, so a Sepsis-3 derivation is noisier.
- **HiRID** is high-resolution data from a Swiss ICU. The extra approval step makes it the slowest of the PhysioNet datasets.
- **SICdb** is from Salzburg and has a similar contributor-approval step.
- **MIMIC-III** is only worth it if you're reproducing an older paper.
- **Data use agreement.** The agreements restrict passing the data to third-party services, which can include online LLM tools. Read this before you paste any records into an AI service.

**Practice data: MIMIC-IV Demo** ([page](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-demo/2.2/)). It has the same schema as MIMIC-IV with 100 patients. Use it this week to write and test your Sepsis-3 labelling code while credentialing is pending. It's too small for training.

## Known, not confirmed

**AmsterdamUMCdb** (Amsterdam UMC, Netherlands) is not registry-verified. The address I tried returned HTTP 404.
- A web search found the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/AmsterdamUMC/AmsterdamUMCdb) and the [Amsterdam Medical Data Science site](https://amsterdammedicaldatascience.nl/).
- Access is free but personal. You complete a training course such as CITI DSOR. You also submit an access request form and end user licence agreement, signed by you and an intensivist reference. After approval you get the data from DANS EASY or Google BigQuery.
- That process comes from search summaries and may have changed. Confirm it on the site.
- There is also a [Sepsis-3 implementation paper](https://gigabytejournal.com/articles/45) and a [PLOS ONE paper on Sepsis-3 epidemiology](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0304133) for this database. The paper is cited in the search results, but I haven't read it.

## Not recommended, and why

- **Hugging Face, Zenodo and figshare "sepsis" records.** These are mostly third-party copies of the 2019 Challenge, or small mortality and biomarker cohorts. Use the official PhysioNet source.
- **Transcriptomic sepsis cohorts** (for example SepsisTensor). They are omics data, not charted vitals and labs.

## What I could not find

- Apart from the 2019 Challenge and the MIMIC-IV demo, I found no open dataset that needs no application.
- I read no PhysioNet processing-time statistics, so "1–2 weeks" is my planning estimate.
- Sizes and table contents for the credentialed datasets are from memory.
- The literature search returned mostly reviews and conference abstracts. I haven't yet attached a specific baseline paper to each dataset, so find those yourself. The [2021 systematic review](https://doi.org/10.3389/fmed.2021.607952) is a place to start.

## Next step

1. **Today:** download the Challenge 2019 data and train your first baseline on it.
2. **Today:** start the CITI course and create your PhysioNet account.
3. **Today:** submit the credentialing application, and ask your supervisor early if you need a reference.
4. **This week:** prototype your Sepsis-3 labelling on the MIMIC-IV demo.
5. **Once approved:** request MIMIC-IV first, then eICU for external validation.
6. **If you want a European cohort:** request HiRID, SICdb or AmsterdamUMCdb in parallel, since those take longer.

All of this was checked on 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12. Access rules and licences change, so recheck them before you rely on them. The interactive page is at `/private/tmp/e-06RH04/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

graders.name: 01-recall-italian-parkinsons-voice-speech
graders.evidence:
I found six public Parkinson's speech datasets with real audio and healthy controls. Five of them you can download today; NeuroVoz needs an access request. I checked each against its registry record on 2026-11-11 or 2026-11-12, except where marked "from memory".

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** actual audio files such as .wav, not precomputed features.
- **R2 (must):** labelled Parkinson's (PD) patients and healthy controls (HC).
- **R3 (nice to have):** downloadable now, without a long approval.
- I assumed any language is fine, since you didn't specify one.

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | VOC-PD (Mandarin) | open download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | 1,551 wav (811 PD, 740 HC), 367 MB | strong | today |
| 2 | MDVR-KCL (King's College London, smartphone) | open download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | 606 MB | strong | today |
| 3 | Italian Parkinson's Voice and Speech (IEEE DataPort) | free account, minutes | CC-BY | 565 MB, wav + xlsx | strong | today |
| 4 | Arabic PD Speech Dataset | open download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | 17 PD + 23 HC, 39 MB | strong | today |
| 5 | NeuroVoz (Castilian Spanish) | request access, days (my estimate) | CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0 | 2,977 audio files | strong | today |
| 6 | Processed MRI + Speech for PD (ParkMultiNet) | open download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | 502 clips, 1.3 GB with MRI | partial | today |

## Details
1. **VOC-PD** (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21775027)
   - It has five task folders: numbers, phrases, sentences, vowels and more.
   - Download the zips from the Zenodo record.
   - It's a 2026 release and nobody has cited it yet.
   - Check the xlsx for speaker IDs so you can split train and test by speaker.
2. **MDVR-KCL** (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.2867215)
   - It has read speech and spontaneous dialogue with early and advanced PD patients, recorded over a phone-quality channel.
   - It has about 3,000 downloads and 17 citations.
   - The cohort is small, roughly 37 speakers. That figure is from memory, not confirmed today.
3. **Italian Parkinson's Voice and Speech** (https://doi.org/10.21227/aw6b-tg17)
   - The IEEE DataPort page says: "Open Access dataset files are accessible to all logged in users." Create a free account, log in and download.
   - Hugging Face holds several uploader copies. Cite and download from IEEE DataPort, not the copies.
   - Which recordings are PD and which are HC is from memory. Check it in the xlsx.
4. **Arabic PD Speech** (https://zenodo.org/records/22036480)
   - It has sustained vowels, a read passage and spontaneous speech.
   - Forty speakers is too few to train on alone. It's useful as a cross-lingual test set.
5. **NeuroVoz** (https://zenodo.org/records/13647600)
   - It has about 27 recordings per participant, from PD patients and controls.
   - Zenodo says: "The record is publicly accessible, but files are restricted." Log in, use "Request access" and accept the Data Usage Agreement.
   - The licence is non-commercial and no-derivatives. Ask the owners whether trained models or augmented audio count as derivatives.
   - One paper that used it is [Multilingual evaluation of interpretable biomarkers in PD speech](https://doi.org/10.3389/fneur.2023.1142642) (2023).
6. **ParkMultiNet** (https://zenodo.org/records/22082939)
   - It's a repackaging of clips from other public sources, plus MRI.
   - It will overlap with other sets, so don't mix it with them in train and test splits.
   - I haven't confirmed whether the clips are waveforms or spectrograms.

## Known, not confirmed
- **PC-GITA** (Colombian Spanish): no registry record found. From memory, it's available from the authors on request only.
- **mPower** (Synapse, smartphone voice): no registry record found. From memory, it needs a Synapse account and a study application.
- **Two figshare sets**: "Parkinson-Disease-voice-Dataset" (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.32588973.v2) and "Dataset for Parkinson Disease" (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.33212514.v1). The DOIs are registered, but figshare blocked my page check. I don't know whether they hold audio.
- **Czech and German corpora**: I didn't search for them.

## Not recommended, and why
- **NeuroVoz Rasta-PLP** on Zenodo is features only.
- **Bridge2AI-Voice on PhysioNet**: the page says "This PhysioNet project does not contain raw audios." Raw audio goes through Synapse and needs institutional sign-off.
- **Synthetic PD voice set** (Zenodo 17753641) is synthetic, not real speakers.
- **BenchmarkDatasets/Parkinson_Speech** on Hugging Face looks like a tabular feature set. I didn't open it to confirm.
- **UCI Parkinson datasets** are feature tables. This is from memory.

## What I could not find
- I searched DataCite, Hugging Face, OpenAIRE, PhysioNet and Zenodo, plus the literature. I did not search project sites or challenge pages, so the list may be incomplete.
- For most datasets I didn't find papers that used them. Only NeuroVoz has one, so you'd need to search for baselines yourself.

## Next step
Start with Italian PVS, MDVR-KCL and VOC-PD. Request NeuroVoz access now so it's ready when you need it. Always split by speaker, because several recordings per person make random splits leak.

   - The licence is non-commercial and no-derivatives. Ask the owners whether trained models or augmented audio count as derivatives.
   - One paper that used it is [Multilingual evaluation of interpretable biomarkers in PD speech](https://doi.org/10.3389/fneur.2023.1142642) (2023).
6. **ParkMultiNet** (https://zenodo.org/records/22082939)
   - It's a repackaging of clips from other public sources, plus MRI.
   - It will overlap with other sets, so don't mix it with them in train and test splits.
   - I haven't confirmed whether the clips are waveforms or spectrograms.
